class.name: ProjectStatics
class.brief_description: Static helpers, currently save game loading and storing.

method.name: clear_load_failure
method.description: Discards the protection [method is_slot_write_blocked] describes, so the next [method save_game] overwrites the slot. Call it when the player has been told their save is unreadable and has chosen to start again - not to make an error message go away.

method.name: get_first_player_controller
method.description: Shorthand for [method World.get_first_player_controller] - player one in a local game, and the only controller a client holds.

method.name: get_game_mode
method.description: Shorthand for [method World.get_game_mode]. Null on a client, where no game mode exists.

method.name: get_game_state
method.description: Shorthand for [method World.get_game_state]. Unlike the game mode, this exists on every peer.

method.name: get_last_load_result
method.description: Why the most recent [method load_game] call returned what it did, whichever slot it was for. [constant LOAD_OK] until the first call. Use it immediately after loading, in the same way [method FileAccess.get_open_error] is used - anything else that loads a slot in between replaces it.

method.name: get_local_player
method.description: Shorthand for [method World.get_local_player] - the humans at this machine, by index.

method.name: get_slot_load_result
method.description: The result this slot last produced, remembered per slot for the life of the process. [constant LOAD_OK] for a slot never read.

method.name: has_save_game
method.description: Whether the slot file exists, without reading or decrypting it. This is the question [method load_game] returning [code]null[/code] cannot answer on its own.

method.name: is_slot_write_blocked
method.description: True while [method save_game] will refuse this slot: it was read this session and failed with something other than [constant LOAD_NOT_FOUND], which means a file is there that nobody could parse. Show the player that their save could not be read, rather than silently starting them over.

method.name: load_game
method.description: Reads back what [method save_game] wrote. Never raises an error, so a bad save cannot stop the game from booting. [b]It returns [code]null[/code] for four different reasons, and [method get_last_load_result] is how you tell them apart[/b] - see [enum LoadResult]. Only [constant LOAD_NOT_FOUND] means "no save yet"; the other three mean a file is sitting there that the player would lose if the game started over and saved on top of it. After any failure other than [constant LOAD_NOT_FOUND] the slot is marked, and [method save_game] refuses to write to it until [method clear_load_failure] is called. So the naive shape - load, and if that gave nothing start fresh and save - no longer destroys the file; it fails loudly on the write instead. [param encrypt] must match what the file was written with.

method.name: save_game
method.description: Serializes [param data] to [code]user://saves/<slot_name>.sav[/code]. When [param encrypt] is true the file is written with the key in [code]application/game_framework/save_encryption_key[/code]. [b]Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_LOCKED] without writing when [method is_slot_write_blocked] is true[/b] - the slot was read this session and could not be parsed, so the file that is there is kept rather than replaced with a fresh profile. [method clear_load_failure] lifts that deliberately. Other failures return the error that caused them; [constant @GlobalScope.OK] means the file was written. [b]That setting defaults to a key that ships with this extension source[/b], so a released game should replace it. The default is kept as it is because changing it makes existing save files unreadable; the framework warns once per run while it is still in use.

constants.constant: The slot was read and deserialized. This is also the value for a slot that has never been read.
There is no file for this slot. [b]The only result that means "first run"[/b] - starting from defaults is correct, and saving is not blocked.
The file exists and could not be opened or decrypted. Most often [code]application/game_framework/save_encryption_key[/code] changed since it was written; the data itself may be perfectly good.
The file was read but its contents were rejected - either the JSON did not parse, or [method SaveGame.from_json] returned an error, which includes a game's own version migration refusing it.
[code]save_game_script[/code] does not extend [SaveGame]. The caller is wrong; the file was never touched.
